items.stem: Who does Antigone first announce is approaching?
options: Creon, coming with his company
Theseus, riding back with armed horsemen
A herald sent from Argos with a truce
A priest assigned to tend the holy grove

items.stem: What does Oedipus say of a man who lives withal content, when Creon urges a return to Thebes?
options: He lives not ill who lives withal content
He will be king of Thebes again this day
He must pay a tribute already named by Creon
He has already asked Theseus to send him home

items.stem: Complete Creon's line: “Command your _____; I am not your slave.”
options: minions
elders
daughters
guests

items.stem: Complete Theseus's command: “Command my _____ leave the sacrifice”
options: prisoners
liegemen
strangers
seers

items.stem: How does Creon first describe his errand to the elders?
options: As persuasion, commissioned by Thebes
As a private visit of simple old friendship
As a direct order issued by King Theseus
As a rite required to cleanse the holy grove

items.stem: What has already happened when Creon first boasts of his power over Oedipus?
options: One daughter is already in his men's hands
Theseus has already had Creon bound in chains
The chorus has already fled and left the grove
Oedipus has already been carried from the sanctuary

items.stem: What does Creon mean by calling the two daughters the crutches that served Oedipus?
options: They were his support in wandering, and Creon means to take that support away
They have already been named joint rulers of Athens in Theseus's stead
They are to serve from now on as priestesses assigned to the holy grove
They will be sent as formal envoys to argue his case at Thebes

items.stem: Why does Theseus rebuke Creon?
options: He broke the law of Athens by using force
He arrived later than he had promised Theseus
He insulted Ismene's travel-worn clothing
He refused to join the sacrifice at the altars

items.stem: What does Theseus command his men to do as soon as he hears of the seizure?
options: Leave the sacrifice and hurry after the maidens
Burn the Theban tents along the whole border road
Arrest Oedipus on a public charge of trespass here
Hand Creon a rich tribute taken from the sacred grove

items.stem: Complete Theseus's line: “For every action _____ of law,”
options: shadow
rumour
warranty
silence

items.stem: Complete the line: “And not by choice a _____; so much”
options: sovereign
sojourner
prisoner
herald

items.stem: Until when does Theseus say Creon may not leave Attica?
options: Until the maidens are fetched and produced in his sight
Until Oedipus agrees at last to travel home with him
Until the chorus has sung Creon all the way out of the grove
Until Apollo sends a second and final sign to Athens

items.stem: How does Oedipus answer the charge of pollution?
options: He acted without knowing what he did
He says Creon alone is guilty of the past
He admits that he planned the deed in full
He says his mother gave him a direct order

items.stem: What is the force of Theseus comparing Creon to a plunderer who carries off what he likes?
options: It presents the seizure as lawless theft, not a lawful embassy
It praises Creon as a soldier doing no more than ordinary duty
It treats the violent act as a completed sacred rite of Thebes
It describes a fair and honoured exchange of guests between cities

items.stem: What does Theseus call Creon's behaviour?
options: Like a freebooter carrying off plunder
Like a king's ordinary and lawful duty
Like a priest completing a required rite
Like a fair exchange of honoured guests

items.stem: Complete Oedipus's line: “But I _____ wed, unwilling speak.”
options: unwitting
eager
angry
open

items.stem: Complete Theseus's line: “_____ and uncorrected at my hands.”
options: Honoured
Scathless
Punished
Welcomed

items.stem: What does Oedipus say Creon has really come to do, rather than take him home?
options: To plant him on Thebes's borders, not to restore him as a free man
To set him on the Theban throne again that very same day
To ask Theseus for a formal military alliance against Argos
To offer him a lasting house inside the walls of Thebes

items.stem: What does Theseus promise Oedipus before leaving with Creon?
options: That he will not abandon his purpose to restore the maidens
That he will send Oedipus back to Thebes at once that day
That he will leave Creon to be judged by the chorus alone now
That he will hide the daughters in a place no citizen may name

items.stem: After persuasion fails, what does Creon's turn to force show about his embassy?
options: He was prepared to take the women if words did not suffice, and he claims them as his
He is surprised by his own men and tries at once to stop the whole seizure
He waits for Theseus's formal leave before anyone is taken from the grove
He offers himself as a willing hostage until the women can be fully heard

items.stem: Complete Theseus's line: “Without _____ or accomplices;”
options: witnesses
abettors
heralds
elders

items.stem: Complete Theseus's line: “I should behave as fits an _____”
options: Athenian
kinsman
suppliant
outlander

items.stem: What does Theseus mean by saying that a single man does not prevail against the State?
options: A private captor, even a prince, cannot overrule the city's law
Oedipus must now be sent away from Athens as a public burden
The chorus, not Theseus, will decide what is next done with Creon
Thebes has already legally claimed both daughters as its very own

items.stem: Why does Oedipus reject Creon's appeal to kinship as a reason to go back?
options: Creon ignored him in exile and now wants him as a tool, not as a free kinsman
Oedipus has already accepted a Theban throne offered by his own sons
Theseus has already forbidden any mention of Thebes inside the grove
Creon has brought the two sons themselves to plead the case in person

items.stem: How does Theseus's image of a fowler taken in the toils he spread work as a warning to Creon?
options: It turns the captor into the one who will be caught by the plot he laid
It praises Creon as a skilled hunter already owed a lawful prize
It means Oedipus should leave the grove and hunt Creon down himself
It predicts that the daughters will choose to go of their own free will now

items.stem: What is Creon doing when he recites Oedipus's past before the Athenians?
options: He is trying to make the city reject the suppliant as polluted, so the seizure will seem justified
He is openly confessing that Thebes was wholly wrong to drive Oedipus out
He is asking the chorus to judge only Creon's own earlier public crimes
He is offering a formal legal pardon if Oedipus will name both of his sons
